title: The Shadow
paragraphs: A crime and mystery series featuring the mysterious Shadow, most famously Lamont Cranston, who uses secrecy, disguise, and the ability to cloud men's minds while battling criminals and protecting the innocent.

Crime/mystery drama built around Lamont Cranston as The Shadow and companion Margo Lane. The dramatic series began September 26, 1937 after earlier radio use of The Shadow as a mysterious narrator. Frozen GRH snapshot has 239 dated recordings through June 27, 1954, six months before the historical finale.

GRH documents the program through Orson Welles lead era (September 26, 1937 to September 18, 1938) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Bill Johnstone lead era (September 25, 1938 to March 21, 1943) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Bret Morrison first lead era (September 26, 1943 to June 30, 1944) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and John Archer lead era (September 1, 1944 to June 30, 1945) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Elsie Thompson (organist on 180 recordings), Ken Roberts (announcer on 138 recordings and performer on 1 recording), William Johnstone (performer on 103 recordings), [[person|bret-morrison|Bret Morrison]] (performer on 93 recordings), Marjorie Anderson (performer on 92 recordings), John Cole (director on 82 recordings and producer on 82 recordings), and Paul Huber (commercial spokesman on 65 recordings and performer on 13 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.666407112636e085|Michelson]] (syndicated by), and [[org|org.50630574777d6937|Don Lee Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include murder and violent crime, supernatural and occult threats, secret identity and disguise, gangs and organized crime, prisons, execution and criminal justice, and mad science and dangerous inventions.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including The Shadow across radio and pulp publishing, Sponsored radio crime drama and premium culture, and Wartime espionage and sabotage themes.
